intents.message: Same quarter of work has to go three places this week: the trustees, the program officer at the foundation that covers about a third of our salaries, and the twelve partner orgs in the cohort. The trustees want the risk picture, the program officer will read it against what we said we'd deliver, and the partners mostly want to know what changed for them. One set of facts, three very different letters.
intents.notes: Anthropic's skill covers exec/engineering/cross-functional/customer/board. A program officer reading against stated deliverables is a funder-reporting act with no analogue in that audience set; 'covers a third of our salaries' is restricted-funding context.

intents.message: Our reporting period closed Friday. I need the narrative that goes back to the three restricted grants — each one only wants the piece of the work its own money paid for — plus a plainer version for the whole staff, and something short enough for the newsletter. Nothing can contradict anything else; last year two of them disagreed on a headcount and it was embarrassing.
intents.notes: Restricted-fund segmentation — reporting only the portion each award financed — has no counterpart in a product-management update skill and is the strongest single discriminator in this pair.

intents.message: Write up the last six weeks for two audiences. One is the family foundation that gave us general operating support and reads three paragraphs at most. The other is our community advisory group, who were actually in the room for most of it and will notice if I smooth anything over.
intents.notes: 'General operating support' is nonprofit finance vocabulary absent from the competitor's entire repo. Community advisory group is a reciprocity audience, not a customer segment.

intents.message: Sprint 14 wrapped. I need the weekly for leadership — RAG status, the two things that slipped and why, and what I need from the platform team. Then a longer cut for the engineers with the actual ticket numbers, and something for the CS folks they can paste to customers who asked about the latency fix.
intents.notes: Pure product-management substrate. If the CIL skill fires here it is winning a contest it should lose, and that is a false positive that degrades the whole bundle's measured routing.

intents.message: We're launching Tuesday. I need the internal announcement, the exec one-pager, and the note that goes to the design partners who've been on the beta.
intents.notes: Launch-announcement shape, explicitly named in the competitor's own description.

intents.message: Trustees meet in two weeks. I need to build what goes in front of them — what's on the agenda, how long each item gets, which items are just noting and which actually need a vote, and what has to be read beforehand. Two of the items touch a director's other organization so I need that handled properly.
intents.notes: Forward-looking packet construction with time allocation, consent-vs-action classification and a conflict-of-interest handling need. The competitor produces the record afterwards and refuses to proceed without a house minutes format.

intents.message: Put together the papers for the finance committee — the year-to-date against budget, where the restricted balances sit, the two policies due for their annual look, and a short cover note so people actually read it before they turn up.
intents.notes: Packet assembly ahead of a committee sitting; restricted balances is nonprofit fund accounting.

intents.message: I've got the recording and the deck from Thursday's board meeting. Draft the minutes in our house format — resolutions carried, abstentions noted, and the written consent we took by email the week before folded in.
intents.notes: Retrospective legal-record production. The CIL skill builds the agenda; if it fires on minutes-drafting it is out of scope.

intents.message: Four staff, no IT person, and we've drifted into using AI for intake summaries, the newsletter and some grant drafting. I don't need a per-tool analysis — I need an honest read on whether we as an organization are anywhere near ready for this, and what the first three things to fix are given nobody here has time.
intents.notes: Organization-level maturity with an explicit capacity constraint, and an explicit rejection of the per-system framing the competitor is built around.

intents.message: Board asked me a question I can't answer: are we behind on this compared to organizations our size. Give me something scored, with a path out, that doesn't assume we can hire anyone.
intents.notes: Peer-relative, capacity-tiered scoring. The competitor scores one system against a regime, not an organization against its cohort.

intents.message: We're deploying a CV-screening model in the EU hiring flow. I need this system classified — are we provider or deployer on it, which risk tier it lands in, and what that triggers before it goes live.
intents.notes: Per-system role-and-tier classification under a regime CIL's set does not cover. Neither CIL skill should fire; the EU AI Act gap is real and the honest answer is out-of-set.

intents.message: Run the impact assessment on the chatbot before the committee sees it — structured intake, the risk analysis, how it classifies under each regime we're in scope for, and a recommendation with conditions.
intents.notes: Single-system impact assessment across regimes — the competitor's exact stated output.

intents.message: Our Texas funder keeps asking whether we follow the federal framework. We run one case-notes tool that matters. Map that tool against the framework properly so I have a memo that stands up, and be explicit about which version you mapped against.
intents.notes: Named framework, single system, memo output, and a version-pinning request — the exact defensive posture the directed NIST revision makes necessary.

intents.message: New guidance dropped last week. Diff it against where our governance posture actually is, flag the gaps, and give me a remediation plan with owners and dates.
intents.notes: Regulation-to-posture diff on arbitrary new guidance. CIL's skill crosswalks a system to one named framework; it should not claim general regulatory diffing.

intents.message: A donor-database company is pitching us an AI add-on. I am not technical and we have no lawyer. What do I actually ask them before we sign, and what answers should worry me?
intents.notes: Buyer-side, pre-contract, explicitly non-technical and unrepresented. The competitor assumes counsel reviewing terms against established governance positions.

intents.message: Here's their DPA and the AI addendum. Review the provisions against our positions — training on our data, liability caps, what happens when they change the underlying model — and flag anything inconsistent with the policy.
intents.notes: Document-in-hand contract review against an existing policy — counsel work, not buyer diligence.

intents.message: We've been using a scoring tool to prioritize who gets into the transitional housing program. Someone raised that it seems to push older applicants down. I need this looked at properly — whether it's actually treating people differently and what we do if it is.
intents.notes: Disparate-impact review of a live consequential-decision system against a protected characteristic. Distinct from a whole-system impact assessment.

intents.message: Before we roll the eligibility model out to the other two sites, I want an honest look at whether it lands differently on the people we serve depending on who they are — and I want it anchored to what the law where we operate actually requires, not just a framework.
intents.notes: Carries the re-anchoring signal: statutory duty over framework language. Worth measuring because the description change proposed for this skill is exactly this move.

intents.message: If the intake assistant ever tells a client something wrong about their benefits, I have no idea what we'd do. Who finds out, who calls the client, who decides whether to switch it off, and what we write down. Build us that, sized for an organization with nine people.
intents.notes: Model-harm incident, not a security incident. Every public IR skill found is cyber/SRE, so the boundary is worth measuring even though no first-party competitor exists.

intents.message: We think there's been unauthorized access to the donor database. Walk me through containment, what we're legally required to notify and by when, and the forensics we should preserve.
intents.notes: A data-breach response, not an AI incident. The AI-specific framing is the skill's whole claim to novelty and it must not dilute into generic breach handling.

intents.message: We can keep the second site open through spring or close it now and put the money into the one that's working. Board wants my recommendation next month. Lay out the real choices and what would have to be true for each to be right.
intents.notes: Consequential organizational choice with a named decision forum. Generic enough that this pair is the one most likely to expose the skill's trigger surface as too broad.

intents.message: Should we go with Postgres or DynamoDB for the events table? Write it up the way we usually record these so the next engineer knows why.
intents.notes: An architecture decision record. Anthropic's `architecture` skill owns this; CIL's should not fire on technical stack choices.

intents.message: Help me think through whether to take the job.
intents.notes: Bare personal deliberation carrying two of the skill's own literal trigger phrases and none of its organizational context. The sharpest available test of whether the description is over-broad.

intents.message: The family foundation asked for two pages before they'll invite a full application. We've never worked with them. Draft it — and do not put a single number in there I haven't given you.
intents.notes: Foundation LOI with an explicit claim-accuracy constraint. Community competitors are NIH/NSF/DoD-shaped and assume a federal notice of funding opportunity.

intents.message: Draft the specific aims page and the biosketch for the R01 resubmission, responding to the reviewer critiques from last cycle.
intents.notes: Federal biomedical research grant. CIL's is foundation philanthropy; the vocabularies do not overlap and neither should the routing.

intents.message: I've lost track of where everything sits. Six funders in play, two of them I think have deadlines this month but I'm not certain and I don't want to trust my own note — and one I may have already missed. Get me straight on what's actually live and what's next.
intents.notes: Multi-funder pipeline state with an explicit deadline-source-verification signal, which is the skill's distinguishing discipline.

intents.message: We fund about forty small organizations and several have started using AI in their programs. I need a consistent way to understand where each of them actually is, without it turning into a compliance burden that punishes the three-person shops for being three-person shops.
intents.notes: Funder-side, portfolio-wide, with the capacity-asymmetry concern stated by the user. Note for the design review: this prompt is also the argument for the no-composite-score rule.

intents.message: Four of us have been running this as a project under another nonprofit's umbrella for two years. It's outgrown that. I want to understand what the actual options are — stay, move to a different arrangement, or stand something up ourselves — and what each would mean.
intents.notes: Entity-structure deliberation framed as options rather than advice. Zero public equivalents found; these cases protect the boundary rather than contest an incumbent.

intents.message: We're registering an association in Lomé and I need to know how the ministry accord works and what it means for receiving European money.
intents.notes: Non-US jurisdiction where the US fiscal-sponsorship instrument does not exist. Confidently recommending a US structure here is the highest-harm failure mode identified in the board review — this case makes it measurable.
